title: Most people read the story of the bronze serpent and miss the moment that could have saved them.
paragraphs: Most people read the story of the bronze serpent and miss the moment that could have saved them.

They remember the snakes.
They remember the judgment.
They remember the strange solution.
In Book of Numbers 21, the people of Israel are dying.

Venom in their veins.
Fire in their blood.
Death spreading from body to body.
“Why have you brought us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness?” (Numbers 21:5)

They despised His provision.
They rejected His leadership.
They mocked His deliverance.
“Then the Lord sent fiery serpents among the people, and they bit the people, so that many people of Israel died.” (Numbers 21:6)
This is where most people get uncomfortable.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…

This wasn’t cruelty.
This was exposure.
The snakes revealed what was already inside them.
God didn’t inject sin into them.
“We have sinned, for we have spoken against the Lord…” (Numbers 21:7)
“Make a fiery serpent and set it on a pole, and everyone who is bitten, when he sees it, shall live.” (Numbers 21:8)

Not touch it.
Not earn it.
Not work for it.

His vision is fading.
His body is collapsing.

“That’s it?
That’s too simple.
That can’t be enough.”

He questions.
He analyzes.
He resists.
Not because there was no cure.
But because he refused the simplicity of it.
Now here’s the part almost everyone misses…
Because in Gospel of John 3:14, Jesus Christ says:
“As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up, that whoever believes in Him may have eternal life.”
So must the Son of Man be lifted up.
And it’s already in your system.

The anger.
The lust.
The pride.
The secret thoughts no one else sees.
“For the wages of sin is death…” (Romans 6:23)
But God has already provided the cure.

Not a system.
Not religion.
Not self-improvement.
And just like in the wilderness—

Not achieve.
Not perform.
Not clean yourself first.
“Believe in the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved.” (Acts 16:31)

So you scroll.
You delay.
You tell yourself “later.”

You don’t reject Jesus because there’s no evidence.
You reject Him because you don’t want to surrender.
Right now, you’re in the same position as those dying in the wilderness.
The solution is already lifted up.
The question is not if it works.
Or will you die analyzing the cure?
If this exposed something in you, don’t ignore it.
